value.hook: Open before diagnosing a watchdog or sweep that did not fire, changing what the death sweep retires, or canarying a launch flag or cargo cap
value.title: Daemon findings from the live store; compaction, reaper and cap lessons

sections.name: body
sections.value:
Learned on F108, F110, F111 (plan 222), F114/F115 and F126 (2026-11-08).

- Diagnose from the live store first, read-only, then confirm from a second origin. Use `sqlite3 "file:$HOME/.pij-rs/pij.sqlite?mode=ro"` (spine_events by seat and seq; watchdog.round outcomes) and the harness's own log (~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl). F108 was a reader ack (delivery.inbox-ack) counting as the seat's own activity; F115 was the dormant-PA digest path never flagging. Both came out of the rows in minutes.
- Compaction leaves no "done" event. Copilot posts nothing after a delivered /compact. Claude's /compact posts exactly one seat.activity idle. So "own activity since X" must exclude idle, and the settle needs a time bound.
- Once-only writes:
  - persist BEFORE admitting (an owned_write survives a dropped caller; refuse if it fails);
  - order by a durable sequence (AUTOINCREMENT), never the wall clock;
  - put the veto inside the marking UPDATE (NOT EXISTS a newer pending row), not in a snapshot taken earlier.
- Destructive rules: name the input that decides (the policy) and each check that can only keep (a brake). Check existing contracts before making anything terminal: a tombstone keeps queued jobs because resume delivers them (the prime's ruling A).
- Per-tick, per-seat reads must not launch. Use the TmuxPort *_without_launch variants (control client only; None means wait), and add one with a real-tmux no-fork test.
- A rule change in the reaper or sweep can break integration witnesses in other binaries (lifecycle_http pinned the old "unknown"). CI's cargo test stops at the first failing binary, so run `-p pij-cli --no-fail-fast` and `-p pij-daemon --tests --no-fail-fast` locally.
- To canary an unmerged launch flag on the live daemon: `pij-rs spawn --bin /tmp/x/<harness>`, where that wrapper execs the real CLI with the flag prepended. Use a control seat without the flag for a positive.
- Cargo caps live in the repo's .cargo/config.toml (jobs 4, RUST_TEST_THREADS 4 force=false). Before trusting such a mechanism, prove it in a scratch crate under `env -i PATH=<toolchain bin>:/usr/bin:/bin`: the build script prints NUM_JOBS, the test prints its env, and removing the config is the control.
